top_story_title: PAN-OS management interfaces exploited through the PHP2Shell pair, both now in KEV
top_story_summary: The two PHP vulnerabilities tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (reported as PHP2Shell) are being used against firewalls. Palo Alto Networks confirmed on October 28 that attackers were exploiting both against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet. Both flaws allow code execution on the web server with no authentication, and both are in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog - added 2026-10-26 with a 2026-10-29 due date, catalogued against PHP Group's PHP rather than under a network vendor's name, which is why they are easy to miss in a vendor-filtered patch process.
top_actions: Enumerate every PAN-OS device whose management interface (HTTPS/SSH/API, including Panorama) answers from the internet, and remove that exposure now - management on a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network only.
Where exposure cannot be removed immediately, restrict the management interface with permitted-IP lists to administrator source ranges and the jump hosts only.
Check the Palo Alto Networks advisory for the fixed release covering CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and schedule the upgrade in the change window, HA pair secondary first.
After patching, rotate local admin credentials, API keys, device certificates and VPN pre-shared keys; terminate active admin and VPN sessions.
Export the configuration and review it for unexpected admin users, modified login pages, new scripts, static routes or tunnels.
executive_summary: Firewalls are the live target: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (PHP2Shell) are in KEV and were confirmed by Palo Alto Networks on October 28 as being exploited against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces.

F5 has two separate problems in one cycle - five NGINX2Root remote code execution flaws with public proof-of-concept exploits, and six critical BIG-IP flaws that let an unauthenticated attacker crash the Traffic Management Microkernel on virtual servers with specific iRule or APM configuration.
Cisco Expressway is being exploited in the wild shortly after a proof of concept went public, against a clustered deployment, with tooling staged for lateral movement.

Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938 in OpenJDK) has moved to active exploit attempts; Cisco has opened an advisory for affected Cisco products but has not yet published the product list, so this needs tracking rather than a one-time read.
SonicWall Gen 6 and Gen 6.5 on SonicOS 6.x is out of support with no further patches regardless of severity - that fleet is now a replacement project, not a patching one.
No fixed release numbers are quoted in this edition where the sources did not state them; confirm every build against the vendor advisory before opening a change.
key_actions: **Palo Alto Networks** — Identify every PAN-OS device and Panorama instance with a management interface reachable from the internet and remove that reachability; management belongs on a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Apply permitted-IP restrictions to the management interface for administrator source ranges and jump hosts where exposure cannot be removed immediately.
**F5** — Check the F5 advisory for the fixed releases and the exact affected versions for NGINX2Root; do not assume a build number from the reporting.
**F5** — Inventory every NGINX and F5 NGINX instance, including ones deployed as containers or inside application stacks, and record the running version - this is where incomplete inventories bite.
**Cisco** — Subscribe to or re-check the Cisco advisory (cisco-sa-nov2026-java-rce) daily until the affected-product and fixed-release tables are populated - the source states it is incomplete.
**Cisco** — Check the vendor advisory for the fixed release; no fixed Cisco versions are stated in the source and none should be assumed.
**SonicWall** — List every Gen 6 and Gen 6.5 unit on SonicOS 6.x with its role, site and whether it terminates internet or VPN traffic; this is the replacement backlog.
**SonicWall** — Move internet-edge and VPN-termination duties off Gen 6 units first - those are the ones SonicWall expects to be targeted.

ai_defenses.solution: Check Point AI Security (agentic steering and automatic agent kill switch)
ai_defenses.what_it_does: Check Point describes AI Security as providing an automatic way to stop an AI agent, held as a last resort, with what it calls agentic steering as the first-line response. The stated rationale is that switching an agent off stops the risk and the work at the same time, so steering an agent away from risky behaviour precedes stopping it.

headlines.title: Everything Is a Web Application, Including Your Firewall
headlines.summary: Palo Alto Networks confirmed attackers exploiting two unauthenticated PHP code-execution flaws against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces.

headlines.title: F5 Patches Critical NGINX2Root Flaws as PoC Exploits Go Public
headlines.summary: F5 patched five NGINX2Root flaws that let remote unauthenticated attackers run code, with proof-of-concept exploits now public.

headlines.title: Vulnerability in Oracle OpenJDK (Java4Shell) Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco is tracking CVE-2026-114938 in OpenJDK (Java4Shell), an RCE in Java 17.0.6 and later on x86-64 that affects an as-yet unlisted set of Cisco products.

headlines.title: SonicWall urges customers to replace Gen 6 firewalls now
headlines.summary: SonicWall Gen 6 and Gen 6.5 firewalls on SonicOS 6.x are now out of support and will get no further patches; SonicWall says replace them and pull them off the edge.

headlines.title: F5 Warns 6 Critical BIG-IP Flaws Can Crash Traffic in Specific Setups, May Allow RCE
headlines.summary: Six critical F5 BIG-IP flaws let an unauthenticated attacker crash the Traffic Management Microkernel and drop traffic on virtual servers with specific iRule or APM config.

headlines.title: Hackers Exploit Cisco Expressway Vulnerability Soon After PoC Release
headlines.summary: Cisco Expressway devices were exploited shortly after a proof of concept went public, with attackers hitting a clustered deployment and staging lateral movement.
